cards.explanation: The answer is the One who ordained it. The LORD says, “Heed the rod and the One who ordained it.” So the call has two parts, friends, the rod and the One behind it. The same verse says it is sound wisdom to fear His name, and I'd say that's worth listening to.

The answer is False. He asks, “Can I forget any longer, O house of the wicked, the treasures of wickedness and the short ephah, which is accursed?” That is not a shrug, friends. It's a question that says He has not forgotten. He then follows it with, “Therefore I am striking you severely, to ruin you because of your sins.” (Micah 6:13)

The answer is dishonest scales and false weights. The LORD asks, “Can I excuse dishonest scales or bags of false weights?” Think of a scale that cheats a little every single time, bakers. It's the kind of thing you'd never want near your cookie box. Back in verse 10 He also names the short ephah, which is accursed.

The answer is the wealthy. The LORD says, “For the wealthy of the city are full of violence, and its residents speak lies…” Just before this, He mentioned the treasures of wickedness (Micah 6:10). Heavy words, friends, and He doesn't soften them.

The answer is True. The LORD says the city's residents “…speak lies; their tongues are deceitful in their mouths.” That fits with the dishonest scales, friends, because crooked words and crooked weights go together. It's one more charge in verse 12, right beside the violence.

The answer is sins. The LORD says, “Therefore I am striking you severely, to ruin you because of your sins.” That word “Therefore” ties it back to the cheating and the lies in the verses before. This is a heavy part, friends, and I won't pretend it isn't.

The answer is that they won't be satisfied. The LORD says, “You will eat but not be satisfied, and your hunger will remain with you.” Imagine sitting down to a full plate and still feeling empty after, bakers. It's the first of several things He lists, and none of them are easy to hear.

The answer is False. The LORD says, “What you acquire, you will not preserve; and what you save, I will give to the sword.” So the saving doesn't hold up, friends. Nothing they stash away stays with them.

The answer is that they won't reap the harvest. The LORD says, “You will sow but not reap…” That's sowing with no reaping to follow, bakers. If I did that with my dough, I'd just stare at a cold oven.

The answers are oil and wine. The LORD says, “you will press olives but not anoint yourselves with oil; you will tread grapes but not drink the wine.” They do all the pressing and the treading, and the oil and the wine never reach them. It's the same pattern as sowing but not reaping, earlier in the same verse. Three times in one verse, friends, and the pattern is clear.

The answer is that they kept them and followed their counsel. Micah 6:16 says the city kept those statutes and followed that counsel. Omri did evil in the sight of the LORD (1 Kings 16:25), and so did his son Ahab (1 Kings 16:30). So the city was walking a road those two had already laid out, friends.

The answer is their scorn. The LORD says, “you will bear the scorn of the nations.” It comes right after He says He will make the city a desolation and its inhabitants an object of contempt. This is a heavy ending, friends. But the passage isn't the whole book, and Micah isn't finished.
